What We Do

Full-Service Laboratory and Pathology Revenue Cycle Management

Laboratory and pathology billing requires precise CPT selection per test methodology, surgical pathology complexity level coding, LCD compliance, and advance determination of coverage for molecular diagnostics. PMEX manages both the clinical lab and pathology sides under one RCM workflow.

Lab CPT and HCPCS Coding

Correct CPT code selected per test methodology, analyte, and panel vs. component rules.

Surgical Pathology Levels

88302 to 88309 complexity levels assigned from the gross and microscopic report findings.

IHC Staining Billing

88342 (initial stain) and 88341 (each additional stain) billed per the pathology report.

Molecular Diagnostics

81200 to 81479 molecular codes billed with gene and variant confirmation.

LCD/NCD Compliance

Coverage determinations checked per test per payer before billing.

ABN Management

Advance Beneficiary Notice issued for non-covered tests before specimen collection.

Sound Familiar?

Common Lab and Pathology Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

Panel code billed when individual component codes reimburse higher under the payer contract.

PMEX evaluates panel vs. component billing per payer and selects the approach that maximizes reimbursement.

Surgical pathology specimen coded at Level IV when the report supports Level VI complexity.

PMEX assigns pathology levels from the report findings, not from specimen type alone.

Lab test submitted without an ICD-10 code on the LCD covered diagnosis list.

PMEX confirms diagnosis linkage against the LCD covered list before submission on every test.

IHC stains not individually billed: only the initial stain submitted, additional stains missed.

PMEX bills 88342 for the first stain and 88341 for each additional stain from the pathology staining record.

Molecular diagnostic test billed without advance determination of coverage from Medicare.

PMEX confirms ADC before specimen enters the molecular workflow on qualifying high-cost tests.

ABN not issued for a non-covered test, eliminating any patient collection option on denial.

PMEX tracks non-covered test patterns and confirms ABN is signed before the specimen is collected.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Lab and Pathology Billing

Clinical labs and pathology groups lose 18 to 30 percent of revenue to diagnosis linkage failures, IHC stain omissions, and molecular authorization gaps.

PATTERN 01

Lab Test Denied, Diagnosis Not on LCD Covered List

Vitamin D test billed. Medicare LCD requires a covered diagnosis such as osteoporosis or chronic kidney disease. General wellness not covered. ABN not issued. No patient collection option created.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX checks every test order against the applicable LCD before billing. When the ordering diagnosis is not on the covered list, PMEX flags the order for ABN issuance before specimen collection.

PATTERN 02

IHC Stains Not Billed Individually

Breast biopsy with ER, PR, HER2, and Ki-67 stains. Only 88342 (initial, $96) billed. Three additional stains (88341 x3, $52 each) not submitted. $156 per case in stain revenue not captured.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX bills 88342 for the initial IHC stain and 88341 for each additional stain, verified against the pathology staining record on every specimen.

PATTERN 03

Molecular Test Denied, No Advance Determination

NGS panel (81455) submitted without Medicare advance determination of coverage. $2,400 claim denied. ADC application not made before specimen accessioning.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX confirms advance determination of coverage for all molecular and genomic tests before the specimen enters the molecular workflow. ADC applications are managed as a pre-accessioning step.

Questions

Lab and Pathology Billing Questions Answered

We evaluate the payer fee schedule and coverage policy. When component codes reimburse more than the panel code under the specific payer contract, we bill components. When the panel code pays higher or is required, we use it.

Levels 88302 to 88309 are based on the complexity of the specimen examination documented in the pathology report. Level VI requires complex multi-tissue examination. We code from report findings, not from specimen type defaults.

We bill 88342 for the first stain and 88341 for each additional stain per the staining record. The stain count is confirmed from the pathology report before submission.

An ABN informs a Medicare patient that a test may not be covered and that they may be billed. It is required before performing a non-covered test if the lab wants the option to collect from the patient on denial.

Yes. We manage billing for hospital outpatient labs, reference labs, independent clinical labs, and anatomic pathology groups.
